text:
Alex Chung: Heads-up — Q1 hosted capacity planning; we need to decide buy/lease/rental mix for EU-edge backfill after the BGP flap last week. Sketch below.
Priya Rao: +1. Do we have updated GPU-hour forecasts for the new generative endpoints? I rolled up usage per-route.
Alex Chung: Short summary: baseline 1.2M GPU-hours/qtr, projected peak 2.1M during planned marketing weeks. Edge/backfill variance adds ~25% in eu-west-1 and ap-southeast-1. Quick numbers below.
Marco Díaz: can you paste the table?
Alex Chung: sure — high level.
```text
scenario, qtr_gpu_hours, peak_factor
baseline, 1_200_000, 1.0
marketing_surge, 2_100_000, 1.75
edge_backfill, +300_000, 1.25
total_peak_est, 2_400_000, 2.0
```
Priya Rao: ok thanks. That suggests we need ~400-600 A100-equivalent GPUs reserved to hit SLOs if we want to maintain ~300ms p50 and sane p95. Is that your calc?
Alex Chung: yes — assuming 32 A100-equivalent nodes pooled with aggressive batching and 2x KV cache warm hit. Operationally that maps to ~300 reserved + 150-250 rented during peak windows.
Lina Park: quick cluster-health note: after the BGP flap we saw KV cache warm failures and a ~7% increase in p99 tail for ~6 hours. Incident: INC-2026-102. We need to factor warm-up time for new backfills.
Jamie O'Neill: that's the core reason for in-region headroom. If we route cross-region during failover, p95 jumps ~2x for retries and network RTT.
Priya Rao: cost sketch: 300 reserved monthly + 200 rented for 6 weeks -> rough delta is $0.85M/quarter vs fully leased $1.1M for same capacity. Rentals use our colo partners (short-term GPU pods).
Marco Díaz: procurement reality: lead time for outright purchase ~10-12 weeks (customs, rack), leases ~2-4 weeks, rentals immediate (but premium). Also warranty/support differences matter for critical SLAs.
Alex Chung: proposal draft: buy 240 GPUs for baseline steady-state, lease 120 for predictable surge capacity, and rely on rentals for episodic marketing surges. Also request targeted network shelf upgrades in eu-west POPs: +10Gbps uplinks to reduce congestion during cross-pop backfills.
Lina Park: noted — opened NET-487 to scope POP uplink upgrades. Current link saturation peaked at ~82% during last surge window (logs attached to ticket).
ops-bot: deploy-checklist: capacity-plan-v1 submitted for eng-infra review. React with :eyes: to ack.
Jamie O'Neill: acked :eyes:. Also want a canary rollout for the new runtime kernels (KV cache warm improvements) across edge nodes to reduce warm failures during spikes.
Priya Rao: I'll update the forecast sheet with the buy/lease/rental scenarios and add a sensitivity row for cold-cache penalties. Link: https://redwood.internal/sheets/q1-capacity
Alex Chung: action items: Alex -> prep procurement ask (spec + cost). Priya -> update sheet with scenarios. Lina -> scope NET-487 + link upgrades. Marco -> confirm rental vendor availability and pricing. Jamie -> canary rollout plan for kernels.
Marco Díaz: on vendor outreach now; I have two vendors that can deliver within 72 hours for rentals.
Alex Chung: thanks team. Let's reconvene Monday 09:00 PT for decision sync. Thread will be used to capture final numbers before procurement. :calendar:
